headline: MORE BEDDING
*ISN'T* BETTER
beats.vo: More bedding under pavers isn't better. Too much can actually make them settle.

headline: ABOUT *1 INCH*,
SCREEDED FLAT
beats.vo: The bedding layer is about *one inch*, screeded flat. That's it.

headline: CAN'T FIX A
*LUMPY* BASE
beats.vo: Extra bedding can't fix a *lumpy base*. The bumps show through over time.

headline: PAVERS GET
*COMPACTED* TOO
beats.vo: After laying, the pavers get *compacted* in, with a protective pad on slabs, then joint sand is swept in and compacted again.
beats.note: bottom-aligned, zoomed about the box centre from 1.34x and panned 40 px left so the worker on the deck at the top-left of the photo stays out of the band (his right edge sits about 45 px outside); effective scale 1.24-1.27x

headline: *FULL JOINTS*,
EVEN SURFACE
beats.vo: That's how you get *full joints* and a tight, even surface.

post.caption: A thicker bedding layer doesn't make pavers stronger; too much can make them settle. On Metro Vancouver patios the bedding layer is about 1 inch, screeded flat, and it can't fix a lumpy base. Then the pavers are compacted in and the joints are filled and compacted again.
post.alt: Real footage of a paver patio being laid on a screeded bedding layer, then close-ups of tight, full paver joints on a pool deck.
